issues.title: Add zone membership and describe geolocation coordinate privacy
issues.author: ramkri123
issues.body:
Two proposals for the Geographic Attestation Results draft:

1) Add an optional zone-membership claim. An operator-defined zone can be a polygon or a set of physical placements. The same Geographic Result could report membership in approved-rooms and also report cabinet 12.

2) Add a privacy paragraph. Explain how a Verifier can establish zone membership without collecting precise coordinates and return only the membership conclusion.

The question about how the result was established appears to be covered by the provenance and evidence-basis proposals in PRs #4 and #6.

Proposed PR text

Zone Membership

The optional grc.zone-membership claim asserts that the Verifier established that the Target Environment was inside the identified zone. Omission conveys no conclusion about membership. A zone can be defined by a geographic boundary, such as a polygon, or by a set of physical placements, such as rooms or cabinets. The claim can appear alone or alongside placement and jurisdiction claims. Any jurisdiction claim requires its own appraisal.

The claim carries an operator-assigned zone-id and a boundary-digest. The digest is the SHA-256 hash of the exact octets of the zone definition used for appraisal. The zone definition’s format and encoding are agreed out of band. A Relying Party using the claim for a policy decision MUST match both values against those expected by its appraisal policy.

Confidentiality Threats

When precise coordinates should be withheld from the Verifier, the Attester can supply Evidence containing or referencing a zero-knowledge membership proof, as in [V-PEA](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-lkspa-rats-verifiable-geo-fence/). The Verifier can appraise the proof without collecting the coordinates and report only membership in the zone used to verify the proof. Zone identifiers, boundary digests, and accompanying placement claims can still reveal location. Verifiers SHOULD disclose only the geographic detail the Relying Party needs.

issues.title: Who defines Zone Membership?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
The text currently says:

````
A zone can be defined by a geographic
boundary, such as a polygon, or by a set of physical placements, such as rooms
or cabinets. The claim can appear alone or alongside the placement and
jurisdiction claims. For example, a Verifier could report membership in an
approved zone spanning several rooms and also report the cabinet number.

The `zone-id` is assigned by the operator and interpreted in a namespace known
to the Verifier and Relying Party.
````

This might be too loose/vague.

pulls.title: fix CDDL label collision + add grc.basis for result strength
pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
Two changes, both against the CDDL in Section 4:

1. `grc.room-number` and `grc.hallway-number` both encoded to label 10 — a CBOR decode collision. Moved `room-number` to 13.

2. Adds an optional `grc.basis` (label 14), addressing #2. Rather than a closed list of positioning techniques (which would need extending every time a new one shows up), it reuses the three roles RFC 9334 already defines and this draft already cites normatively: `evidence` (the Attester itself produced the location — a signed GNSS fix, or the proximity measurement in Appendix A), `endorsement` (a third party vouches for it — e.g. a cloud provider's signed statement about a rack), `attestation-result` (a Verifier computed or inferred it — e.g. an operator-selected console region label, which today carries none of the strength of the first two but is indistinguishable from them in the current claims map). An optional `ref` points a Relying Party at the specific supporting claim by digest without embedding it, mirroring how draft-ietf-rats-endorsements keeps Endorsements separate from the Evidence they support.

Verified against a clean build: baseline idnits was 4 errors / 1 flaw / 3 warnings (all pre-existing, unrelated to this section); after this change, identical counts, nothing new introduced. The `&(...)` group-to-choice syntax follows RFC 8610 §2.2.2.2 verbatim.

Happy to adjust the label numbers or field names if you'd rather go a different direction — this is meant to open the specific design question in #2, not settle it.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body:
The CDDL on this branch does not parse. With `eat.JC<J,C>` stubbed, using the `cddl` gem 0.12.14:

```
$ cat t.cddl
eat.JC<J, C> = C
grc.claim-uuid = eat.JC("corim.uuid-type", 12>

$ cddl t.cddl generate
*** Look for syntax problems around the %%% markers:
grc.claim-uuid = eat.JC%%%("corim.uuid-type", 12>
*** Parse error at 40 upto 40 of 64 (1410).
```

Lines 229 and 230 open the generic argument list with `(` and close it with `>`. Changing `(` to `<` on both fixes it — the `>` is already right. Control: `eat.JC<"corim.uuid-type", 12>` parses and emits `12`.

Fixing the delimiter surfaces two more inside the same five added lines:

```
Duplicate rule definition grm.provence
  -- old: >eat.JC<"grc.provence-values", 13>"]<  (line 230)
  -- new: >tstr .size 8"]<                       (line 233)

Unknown type grc.provence-values
  referenced at line 198, never defined
```

Separately, on the value type. `tstr .size 8` is exactly 8 bytes, so it rejects every form the Provenance Values section mandates:

```
x = tstr .size 8
  "RFC9711"        -> REJECT   (7)
  "RFC123456"      -> REJECT   (9)
  "I-D.something"  -> REJECT   (13)
```

`tstr / uint` accepts all three, and also the bare integer form the section describes.

Rebase note: the base here is `6c12383`, so this branch still carries `grc.hallway-number` and `grc.room-number` both at label 10. On current main `room-number` is 12, and 13 upward are free.

One naming thing, lowest priority: the CDDL spells `provence` while the section heading and registry name spell `Provenance`. The prose is already right.

pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
Draft, stacked on #6, 41 lines of text, one short example, no code or data. Delete-able as a unit.

**basis-ref (label 16, uuid).** The `claim-uuid` of the result this one rests on. MUST be present when `basis` is `attestation-result` and the consumed result carried a `claim-uuid`; without it the class is a dead end for an auditor. Distinct from `near-to`, which is spatial.

**observed-from / observed-until (labels 17, 18, time).** The interval the observations behind the result cover. A conclusion drawn from a trajectory is about a period, not an instant; the EAR's issue time does not say which period.

Label 15 is left free for the provenance value of #4 (which, as written, uses 13, the label #6 uses for claim-uuid).

The one example is a 57-byte result resting on another result, with the reference and the interval, in diagnostic notation, and a sentence on where it came from. The producer's own data and analysis stay with the producer's document, as suggested; the chain that produced the bytes is at https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/geoar-verifier.

pulls.title: Security Considerations: relayed Results and masked platform identities
pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
Two short subsections under Security Considerations, as promised on the list (11 September) after Usama Sardar's questions and Giri Mandyam's answer on CHIP_ID.

**Relayed Results.** A geographic Attestation Result states where the Attester's platform was found, not where the Relying Party's peer is; an Attester elsewhere can present a genuine Result obtained by a platform in the attested place (the diversion attack of Sardar, Moustafa and Aura, ASIA CCS 2026, Section 8). The text asks the Relying Party to require that the Evidence behind the Result be bound to the session through a value derived from the session's shared secret (the TLS exporter value of RFC 9266, in the freshness field of the Evidence) and the Verifier to carry that binding into the Result; it says explicitly that binding to a public key alone does not correlate the Evidence with the session, per the binder analysis in ID-Crisis. Measured on 11 September (geoar-verifier, PROTOCOLS.md, protocol 5): through a relay holding the guest's TLS key the key binder accepts and the exporter binder rejects.

**Masked platform identities.** MaskChipId zeroes CHIP_ID in every guest report and VCEK_DIS makes the report key shared across a provider's key domain (SEV-SNP ABI, Rev. 1.58, Sections 3.7, 7.3, 8.18); measured on AWS shared tenancy on 11 September. Per Giri's note on the list, a zeroed identity is an appraisal-policy input, not an error; the text says what it implies for the basis of the Result. Written without reference to the `basis` field so that it applies whether #6 or #4 lands.

References added (informative): ID-Crisis, SNP-ABI, RFC9266. Builds with kramdown-rfc and xml2rfc.

---
Update pushed 11 September (evening), commit 34fdbf0, after Usama Sardar's reply of 19:56Z:

- Relayed Results: the binder analysis is now cited where it lives, Intra-handshake.fail (ESORICS 2026, binding mechanisms 4 and 6), and the text says a public-key binding fails against any other holder of the private key, not only a leaked one; the public key MAY accompany the shared-secret-derived value (its Section 7.2). ID-Crisis stays as the reference for the diversion attack.
- Masked Platform Identities: MaskChipId and VCEK_DIS are independent host choices, neither visible in the report except by its effect; a per-chip signature with a zero CHIP_ID is verifiable only by whoever learns the chip identity from the host side, which makes that certificate an operator statement; the shared key names the provider's fleet without the chip, the per-chip key the chip without the provider (SNP-ABI Section 3.7).
- Measured on 11 September on a bare-metal EPYC Genoa under my control, four launch configurations (geoar-verifier, baremetal/RESULTS.md).

pulls.title: One numbering for the CDDL and the examples; examples/ with a Makefile
pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
After the merges of 14 November the document carried three numberings.
This puts it back on one and adds the script you asked for.

## What was wrong on main (48963c2)

- The CDDL had claim-uuid 14 and basis 15. The bytes of the three examples had 13 and 14. The notation of the first two examples said 14 and 15 above bytes that say 13 and 14.
- provence had label 12, which is room-number. Its line opened the generic with a parenthesis, `eat.JC("grc.provence-values", 12>`, so the block did not parse, and `grc.provence-values` had no definition.
- With the numbers as merged the CDDL rejected all three examples.

## What this does

Three commits. Each can be read alone, and the first one stands without the other two.

1. **The numbers.** claim-uuid 13, basis 14, provence 15. 13 and 14 are the numbers in the bytes of the examples, in the slides and in the vectors of the Verifier that the appendix names. 15 is the number that #7 had left for provence. The provence line parses, its JSON name follows the other labels (`"grc.provence"`), and its value is `tstr / uint`, the two forms that the Provenance Values registry describes. Labels 0 to 19 are each used once.
2. **Files.** The CDDL moves to `cddl/geographic-results.cddl` and the examples to `examples/`. The document includes them with `{::include}`, the way draft-ietf-rats-ear keeps its CDDL and its examples. The text rendering is byte for byte the one after commit 1.
3. **The script.** `make -C examples` derives each `.hex` file from its `.edn` file with `diag2cbor.rb` and then checks four things: each result validates against the CDDL of the document; each `.hex` file is the encoding of its `.edn` file; each annotated listing holds those same bytes (`pretty2cbor.rb`); and the three maps that the appendix names as rejected are rejected. One line of the document changes: the 36-byte encoding is now on two lines.

If you prefer 14 and 15 for claim-uuid and basis, it is a change of two numbers in the CDDL and in the three `.edn` files, then `make`, then the two `.pretty` files where `make` points. The slides would need the same change.

## How it was verified

- `make -C examples`: 11 checks pass (cbor-diag 0.11.8, cddl 0.12.14).
- The checks themselves: 13 single changes, each of which must make `make check` fail, and each does. Among them: a label moved in an example or in the CDDL, one byte changed in a `.hex` or in a `.pretty` file, a rejected map made valid, a file that is not notation.
- The document builds with kramdown-rfc 1.7.43 and xml2rfc 3.34.1. The text differs from main only in the lines named above. The warning about the 72-character line of bytes is gone.
- On a private copy of the repository the build of the Editor's Copy is green for this branch, and `make -C examples` passes on Linux as well (GNU Make 4.3, ruby 3.3, the same versions of the two gems).

## What the check does not cover

No example carries provence, zone-membership or the placement claims, so the check does not exercise them.
The numbers in the comments of the `.pretty` files are written by hand; the check compares their bytes.

## Seen on the way, not changed

- The CDDL uses `non-empty` and neither defines nor imports it. `cddl/imports.cddl` carries the definition that draft-ietf-rats-ear uses.
- The CDDL spells `provence`. The section and the registry spell Provenance.
- The JSON name of the subdivision label is `"grc.jurisdiction-state"`. The other names say subdivision.
- The check is not hooked into the build of the document, so the build needs no new gems. draft-ietf-rats-ear hooks its check in with a Gemfile. Say the word and I add the same here.

The proof-reading pass that the adoption call asked for.

One commit: spelling and typing slips in 50 lines, over the whole text.
None of them changes what the document says.
Two are in the references: the link for IEEE 802.1AR ended in a stray `l` and returned 404, and the name of the ISO.

- The claim list of the section "Claim definition" does not name claim-uuid, basis, basis-ref, observed-from, observed-until or provence.
- Claim list, item 6: `jurisdiction-city-exclave = state-specific-list`. The CDDL has `bool`.
- Claim list, item 13: `floor-number = string`. The CDDL has `int`.
- "The series of claims, Data-Center, Floor-Number, ...": no Data-Center claim is defined.
- Proof of Presence: "a 33 byte nonce, base64URL encoded into a 45 byte string". 33 bytes encode to 44 characters.
- Security Considerations of the appendix: "the device SHOULD not respond". SHOULD NOT?

pulls.author: thomas-fossati
pulls.body: Replace the reference to ID crisis (and large part of the related prose) with a reference to §5 of the seat-use-cases draft, which provides a more general set of requirements for an attested secure channel

reviews.author: nikolaichuk7
reviews.body:
Agreed, and thank you.

Section 4.3.2 of the SEAT use cases is the relay of our figure, and it covers a case that the paragraph I wrote did not: the platform in the attested place produces Evidence that carries the binder of the attacker's connection. The exporter value alone does not stop that. Section 5.2 states what is needed in general terms, so the reference is the better home for it.
